fields.name: nav
fields.label: Navigation
fields.description: Menu labels. The destination of each link is set in code — reordering or renaming here changes what a visitor reads, not where it goes.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Link (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which menu entry this is. Read-only: changing it would stop the label applying to that menu item.

fields.name: closingCta
fields.label: Closing CTA band
fields.description: The dark band above the footer. It ends every page on the site.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading
fields.description: A line break in this field becomes a line break on the page.

fields.name: reassurance
fields.label: Reassurance line
fields.description: The small print under the button.

fields.name: backgroundImage
fields.label: Background image
fields.description: The photograph behind this band. It sits under a dark wash so the white text stays readable, so a busy or very pale image still works. This band ends every page on the site, so it is the most-seen image here.

fields.name: backgroundAlt
fields.label: Background image description
fields.description: Describes the photograph for screen readers and search engines. Not shown on the page.

fields.name: email
fields.label: Email address
fields.description: Shown as text and used as the mailto: link. Both come from this one field.

fields.name: phone
fields.label: Phone number
fields.description: Shown as text and used as the tel: link. Type it as it should read, e.g. "0808 175 5405"; the dialling form is derived from it.

fields.name: testimonials
fields.label: Reviews section
fields.description: The band of Trustpilot reviews, shown on several pages.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: Small label above the heading. Default when a page does not set its own.

fields.name: lede
fields.label: Supporting line
fields.description: The current line ("Every review on our Trustpilot profile is five star") is a checkable factual claim rather than a score — keep it true if you change it.

fields.name: linkLabel
fields.label: Link label
fields.description: Text of the link out to the full Trustpilot profile. The URL itself is set in code.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Hero
fields.description: The full-height opening section. The background film is set in code (it is hosted on Vimeo); the still image behind it, which is what shows on phones and before the film loads, is editable below.

fields.name: badge
fields.label: Badge
fields.description: The small pill above the headline, next to the green dot.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: A line break in this field becomes a line break on the page. Ed’s August 2026 final brief set this as "Feasibility-First Architecture", with "Nationwide" kept in the supporting paragraph rather than forced into the headline.

fields.name: primaryCtaLabel
fields.label: Main button label
fields.description: Goes to the pricing calculator. The destination is set in code.

fields.name: secondaryCtaLabel
fields.label: Second button label
fields.description: Goes to the feasibility package page. The destination is set in code.

fields.name: reassurance
fields.label: Reassurance line
fields.description: The small print under the buttons.

fields.name: videoId
fields.label: Background film
fields.description: Paste the Vimeo link for the film, or just its number. Both work — the Share link, the Embed link, or the id on its own. Leave it empty and the hero shows the still image alone, which is what phones and anyone who has asked for reduced motion see anyway. The film always plays silently, on a loop, with no player controls and no tracking; that part is fixed and is not something a different link can change.

fields.name: posterImage
fields.label: Background image
fields.description: The still behind the hero. It is what visitors see on phones, and before the film loads on desktop, so it should read well on its own. A wide landscape photograph works best — it is cropped to fill the screen.

fields.name: posterAlt
fields.label: Background image description (alt text)
fields.description: Not visible on the page. Screen readers read it aloud, and it shows if the image fails to load, so describe what the still behind the film shows.

fields.name: metrics
fields.label: Impact numbers
fields.description: The three cards along the bottom of the hero. These are factual claims a reader can ask you to stand behind: the 98.5% planning success rate and the 86% faster figure are both still flagged unconfirmed in docs/case-study-confirmations.md and docs/dns-migration.md, and the identical 86% claim has already been replaced on the About page. On the 2026-08-25 call Ed gave "350 plus feasibilities" and "500 plus completed projects", which are his own numbers and safer to publish.

fields.name: detail
fields.label: Qualifier
fields.description: The small grey line underneath, which says what the number is measured against.

fields.name: logos
fields.label: Developer logo strip
fields.description: The scrolling band of client logos under the hero. The logo images themselves are set in code — each row below names one of them and carries only its wording.

fields.name: items
fields.label: Logos
fields.description: Neither field here is visible on the page — the logo image is. They are what a screen reader announces, and what a search engine reads in place of a picture of a name.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Logo (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which logo image this row belongs to. Read-only: changing it would attach the wording to the wrong logo.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Company name
fields.description: Also used as the image description unless you set one below. Goldgate Properties is spelt the way its own logo spells it, not "Goldengate" as it appeared on Ed’s list.

fields.name: alt
fields.label: Image description (alt text)
fields.description: Only needed where the company name alone would not describe the image. Leave empty to use the name.

fields.name: projects
fields.label: Example projects
fields.description: The three project cards. Everything printed on a card — image, title, location, tag — comes from the case study itself and is edited there; pick which studies appear, and the wording around them, here.

fields.name: featured
fields.label: Featured case studies
fields.description: The three studies shown on the homepage, in this order. Picked from the case studies rather than typed, so one cannot be named here and then not exist. The band is built for three: fewer leaves a gap in the row, more overflows it. Clearing the list restores the three it shipped with rather than emptying the section.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading
fields.description: A line break in this field becomes a line break on the page.

fields.name: buttonLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: The link through to all the work. Its destination is set in code.

fields.name: stageLines
fields.label: Stage lines
fields.description: The short green line on each card, from Ed’s August 2026 final brief, section 01: "add a subtle stage or outcome line where useful". It summarises facts that already live on the project (status, units, recommendation), written per card here rather than stored on the project itself.

fields.name: slug
fields.label: Project (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which card this line sits on. Read-only: it has to match the case study’s own web address.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading, second line (green)
fields.description: Two fields because the second line is picked out in green.

fields.name: steps
fields.label: Steps
fields.description: The icon on each step is set in code, by position: the first step gets the upload icon, the second the phone, and so on. Reordering the steps here moves the wording but not the icons. The last step in the list is always the one given the full width and the green treatment.

fields.name: num
fields.label: Step number
fields.description: Shown large beside the icon. Ed’s video feedback 2026-07-08: step numbers must read clearly at a glance.

fields.name: bridge
fields.label: Closing paragraph
fields.description: Ed’s August 2026 final brief asked for one short bridge after the five steps, so the architecture side of the practice stays visible without a services section.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: The button under the steps. Its destination is set in code.

fields.name: seo
fields.label: Search engine listing
fields.description: Not visible on the page. This is what Google and link previews show. Leave both empty and the homepage keeps the site-wide defaults, which were written for this page anyway.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Title
fields.description: Empty means the site-wide default, "Thistle Architecture | Feasibility Solved". Anything typed here is used exactly as typed, with no "| Thistle Architecture" added on the end, so include it yourself if you want it.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Description
fields.description: Empty means the site-wide default, "Data-driven feasibility for commercial conversions, HMOs, and high-end residential across the UK." Google shows roughly the first 155 characters.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "About". Around 50 characters works best.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small grey word above the headline.

fields.name: intro
fields.label: "Who We Are" section
fields.description: The photo and two paragraphs directly under the page header. Ed's August 2026 final brief asked for this to be about the practice rather than about the team buying and investing in buildings — the development experience is supporting credibility in the second paragraph, not the headline.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading (first line)
fields.description: Shown in black, on its own line.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading (second line, green)
fields.description: Shown in green underneath the first line. Both lines always appear; clearing this box restores the wording that is there now rather than removing the line.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Photograph
fields.description: The section is "Who We Are", so this wants to be the people, not a building. The current shot is from the August 2026 studio session; it replaced a strip-out photo of Beauchamp House, which said more about the work than about who does it.

fields.name: imageAlt
fields.label: Photograph description (alt text)
fields.description: Read aloud to blind visitors and used by Google; it is never shown on the page. Describe what is actually happening in the photo. Change it whenever you change the photo.

fields.name: themes
fields.label: Core themes
fields.description: The row of small cards under "Who We Are". These are the five core themes from Ed's August 2026 final brief, section 07. The row is designed for five across; adding a sixth wraps it onto a second line.

fields.name: stats
fields.label: Figures band
fields.description: The three figures in the black band. Every one of these is a public claim about the practice, so only put a number here you could evidence if a client asked. The band is built for three; a fourth will not sit evenly.

fields.name: value
fields.label: Figure
fields.description: The large text, e.g. "98.5%".

fields.name: label
fields.label: What it means
fields.description: The small line underneath.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading (first line)
fields.description: Shown in black, on its own line.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading (second line, green)
fields.description: Shown in green underneath the first line. Both lines always appear; clearing this box restores the wording that is there now rather than removing the line.

fields.name: members
fields.label: Team members
fields.description: The cards run three to a row, so a roster of six fills two rows evenly. Onaiza is not on the page: there is no photograph of her and she is not on the live site either.

fields.name: role
fields.label: Job title
fields.description: Optional, and left blank on purpose where nobody has confirmed a title. Please do not invent one — a card with no title is better than a title that turns out to be wrong. Whatever is here is also read aloud to blind visitors as part of the photo description.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Photograph
fields.description: Portrait, cropped to 4:5. Five of the six are from the August 2026 studio shoot, all facing camera against the same background so the cards read as one set; Beverley supplied her own because she was not there on the day, and should be photographed next time. Use a real photograph, never an AI-generated one.

fields.name: contribution
fields.label: What they contribute
fields.description: Ed's August 2026 final brief: write this around what the person contributes to projects, not as a CV-style list of previous jobs.

fields.name: credential
fields.label: Qualification line
fields.description: Optional. The small grey line at the bottom of the card, for confirmed qualifications only, e.g. "BArch in Architecture". Leave it blank rather than guessing.

fields.name: reviews
fields.label: Reviews heading
fields.description: Just the two lines above the Trustpilot reviews on this page. The reviews themselves, and the supporting line and link under the heading, are edited under "Reviews" and "Site Settings".

fields.name: closing
fields.label: "How We Work" section
fields.description: The centred statement that closes the page, above the standard CTA band.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "Feasibility Package". Around 50 characters works best.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters. This is the page people find when they search for a feasibility study, so it is worth the time.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Hero
fields.description: The full-height photograph at the top, with the headline and the first call to action over it.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the headline.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: The only h1 on the page. Press Enter where you want the line to break — it currently breaks after "Answered", and the break is part of the design rather than an accident of screen width.

fields.name: priceHeadline
fields.label: Price line
fields.description: The larger of the two price lines. Ed's August 2026 final brief asked for exactly this shape: "Feasibility from £49.99" with "Architect-led feasibility from £298" immediately below. This line quotes a price. The number here is only the wording — it does not change what anyone is charged, which is set in code next to the pricing engine. If a price changes, ask the developer to move both together, rather than editing this on its own.

fields.name: priceSub
fields.label: Second price line
fields.description: The quieter line under it, for the architect-led fee. This line quotes a price. The number here is only the wording — it does not change what anyone is charged, which is set in code next to the pricing engine. If a price changes, ask the developer to move both together, rather than editing this on its own.

fields.name: lede
fields.label: Supporting paragraph
fields.description: The sentence under the prices, above the button.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: The main call to action. It scrolls to the product choice further down this page; where it goes is set in code, so only the wording is editable here.

fields.name: ctaNote
fields.label: Note under the button
fields.description: The small reassurance line. It promises a response time, so only change it to one the team can actually meet.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Background photograph
fields.description: Sits behind a dark overlay, so it wants to be a finished building with a clear silhouette rather than anything with detail to read. The current shot is the completed Bereweeke Avenue house.

fields.name: imageAlt
fields.label: Photograph description (alt text)
fields.description: Read aloud to blind visitors and used by Google; it is never shown on the page, so it cannot be clicked on the page either. Describe what is actually in the photo, and change it whenever you change the photo.

fields.name: markers
fields.label: Trust markers
fields.description: The three ticked claims along the bottom of the hero. Each one is a public promise, so only put something here the practice could evidence if a client asked. The row is built for three; a fourth wraps onto its own line. The icons are set in code and pair with these by position.

fields.name: entry
fields.label: "Choose Your Route" section
fields.description: The two product cards near the top of the page per Ed's August 2026 final brief: "the website should never feel like contact us for a quote". The name/email/phone form on the £49.99 card is the mechanic rather than copy and is set in code. The fee calculator itself lives on the pricing page only, since September 2026.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading
fields.description: The large line. This line quotes a price. The number here is only the wording — it does not change what anyone is charged, which is set in code next to the pricing engine. If a price changes, ask the developer to move both together, rather than editing this on its own.

fields.name: priceSub
fields.label: Second line under the heading
fields.description: The quieter architect-led price line under it. This line quotes a price. The number here is only the wording — it does not change what anyone is charged, which is set in code next to the pricing engine. If a price changes, ask the developer to move both together, rather than editing this on its own.

fields.name: automated
fields.label: Automated Site Feasibility card
fields.description: The left-hand card. Its price is set in code, beside the code that actually takes the payment, so it cannot be edited here — see the note at the top of this collection.

fields.name: strapline
fields.label: One-line summary
fields.description: The bold line under the price. It states a turnaround, so keep it to one the team can meet.

fields.name: includes
fields.label: What is included
fields.description: The ticked list. These are what the automated report actually contains, so add a line only when the report really covers it.

fields.name: architectural
fields.label: Architectural Feasibility card
fields.description: The right-hand, preferred card. Its price is set in code for the same reason as the other one.

fields.name: badge
fields.label: Badge
fields.description: The small tab on the top edge. Ed's brief asks for the architect-led product to be the visually preferred option, labelled explicitly.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: Opens the fee calculator on the pricing page. Where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: partnerPrefix
fields.label: Partner note: opening
fields.description: The faint line under the calculator, before the link. Ed asked that the £15.99 HMO check is not used as the main feasibility headline and is clearly marked as a partner offer, which is why it sits here rather than in the cards above.

fields.name: partnerLinkLabel
fields.label: Partner note: link text
fields.description: The linked words in the middle of that line. The link goes to hmochecker.co.uk, which is set in code. This line quotes a price. The number here is only the wording — it does not change what anyone is charged, which is set in code next to the pricing engine. If a price changes, ask the developer to move both together, rather than editing this on its own.

fields.name: partnerSuffix
fields.label: Partner note: closing
fields.description: The rest of the sentence after the link. It is what makes clear the tool is a partner product and not an architectural feasibility, so keep that distinction in whatever you write.

fields.name: howItWorks
fields.label: "Five Days, Five Steps." section
fields.description: The numbered timeline, absorbed from the old How It Works page.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading (first line)
fields.description: Shown in black, on its own line.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading (second line, green)
fields.description: Shown in green underneath the first line. Both lines always appear; clearing this box restores the wording that is there now rather than removing the line.

fields.name: steps
fields.label: Steps
fields.description: In order down the page. The circled numbers are counted from the order of this list, so there is nothing to renumber — but the heading above says "Five Steps", so change that too if you add or remove one.

fields.name: durationLabel
fields.label: How long it takes
fields.description: The small green line above the step title. These durations are a proposal and were flagged for confirmation with the client, so check one before treating it as a promise.

fields.name: detail
fields.label: Second paragraph
fields.description: The smaller grey paragraph. Steps 1 and 5 describe how the deposit and the five-day clock work, and the brief defines that clock as starting once both payment and the full project brief are in. Do not restate it as starting from payment alone.

fields.name: deliverables
fields.label: "What You Actually Receive" section
fields.description: The five deliverables, the sample-report request, and the nine-bed HMO example, merged into one section per Ed's August 2026 final brief.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading (first line)
fields.description: Shown in black, on its own line.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading (second line, green)
fields.description: Shown in green underneath the first line. Both lines always appear; clearing this box restores the wording that is there now rather than removing the line.

fields.name: items
fields.label: The five deliverables
fields.description: Each deliverable's "why it matters" line and the document shown beside it. The deliverable NAME and its one-line description are deliberately not here: the /conversions pages render the same five names and descriptions from the same place in code, so editing them here would leave the two sets of pages disagreeing. Ask the developer if one needs renaming.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Deliverable (fixed)
fields.description: The deliverable this row belongs to. Read-only: it is how the page finds the right row, so changing it would stop your edits on this row from showing.

fields.name: why
fields.label: Why it matters
fields.description: The second paragraph, shown when this deliverable is the one selected. This is the sell, not the description.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Document shown beside it
fields.description: A real page from a real report — all five are from 155 Windmill Lane, the example project Ed nominated, and they replaced stock images he described as wrong and muddled on 5 August. Use a page of the document this deliverable actually produces. It is shown whole rather than cropped, so a full page reads correctly.

fields.name: imageAlt
fields.label: Document description (alt text)
fields.description: Read aloud to blind visitors and used by Google; never shown on the page. Say what the document shows, not just what it is called.

fields.name: sample
fields.label: Sample report request
fields.description: The white card offering a full sample feasibility by email. The email box, its button and its messages are the mechanic and are set in code; the wording around them is here.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Paragraph
fields.description: This promises the sample has the client details removed. It does, because the un-redacted version was taken down for exactly that reason, so keep the promise in whatever you write.

fields.name: privacyNote
fields.label: Note under the box
fields.description: The small grey line about what happens to the address. It is a promise about follow-up, so only say what the team will actually do.

fields.name: example
fields.label: "See It In Practice" card
fields.description: The small card at the bottom pointing at one real project. Which project, its title, its description and its photograph all come from the case study itself, so only these two lines are here.

fields.name: linkLabel
fields.label: Link text
fields.description: The link into the case study. Where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: analysis
fields.label: "What's Included In Data Analysis" section
fields.description: The six analysis layers, each with a drawn diagram. The diagrams are drawn in code from the brand palette, and the sample figures inside them (the £3.2M GDV, the 22 HMOs, the eight units) are illustrative rather than a real project — they are not editable, because a number typed into one would read as a claim.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading (first line)
fields.description: Shown in black, on its own line.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading (second line, green)
fields.description: Shown in green underneath the first line. Both lines always appear; clearing this box restores the wording that is there now rather than removing the line.

fields.name: layers
fields.label: Layers
fields.description: The six cards, in order. All three lines of a card are edited here together — before this collection existed the layer name lived in one file and its description in another, and the two could drift apart. Each card is paired with its diagram by position, and there are six diagrams, so a seventh layer would appear with an empty frame.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Layer number
fields.description: The small green "Layer 01" line. It is typed rather than counted, so renumber the rest if you reorder them.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: The button under the six cards. It scrolls back up to the calculator; where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: team
fields.label: "Who You're Working With" section
fields.description: Three people, not the whole roster: Ed's August 2026 final brief asks to "make Edward and Kaan part of the reason to buy the architect-led service", with Jodi as the first point of contact for Expert Sessions. The full team is on the About page and is edited there.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: people
fields.label: People
fields.description: Three across, so a fourth would start a second row. Photo descriptions are built from the name and job title, so there is nothing separate to keep in step.

fields.name: line
fields.label: Why they matter here
fields.description: What this person contributes to a feasibility, in Ed's own framing rather than as a CV. Ed's own line quotes figures about his track record; only keep a figure that could be evidenced if a client asked.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Photograph
fields.description: Optional. Where there is no photograph the card shows the person's initials instead, which is deliberate — Jodi has no photo in the client's Team Photos folder, and inventing or borrowing one is worse than initials. Use a real photograph, never an AI-generated one.

fields.name: proofPoints
fields.label: Credibility line
fields.description: The faint dotted line under the three cards. Ed's brief asks for "concise credibility proof such as hundreds of conversions designed, nationwide project experience, planning success and core project types" — phrased generally on purpose, rather than borrowing HMO Designers' project counts, which are a different business's numbers.

fields.name: linkLabel
fields.label: Link to the About page
fields.description: The link under the credibility line. Where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: reviews
fields.label: Reviews heading
fields.description: Just the eyebrow above the Trustpilot reviews on this page. The reviews themselves are edited under "Reviews", the supporting line and the link label under "Site Settings", and the heading is the shared one every page with this band uses. Maywood Group leads here, pinned in code: their review is about booking a feasibility before committing to a purchase, and about the study returning an answer they did not want, which argues for the product better than any wording of ours.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: The button beside the questions. Where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: items
fields.label: Questions
fields.description: In order down the page; the first one is open when the page loads. Several of these commit the practice to something — the fee being fixed either way, VAT being included, one round of revisions, the five-day clock. Check a commitment still holds before changing how it is worded.

fields.name: exclusions
fields.label: Bulleted list under the answer
fields.description: Optional, and used by one question only: what is not in the fixed fee. Anything left off this list is something a client can reasonably expect to be included, so it is a scope document as much as a FAQ.

fields.name: stickyCta
fields.label: Mobile sticky bar
fields.description: The black bar pinned to the bottom of the screen on phones once the hero has scrolled past. The price in it is set in code, next to the pricing engine.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: This bar is narrow at 320px, so a long label pushes the price line onto two. Keep it about as short as the wording that is there now.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Browser tab title
fields.description: Shown in the browser tab. This page is deliberately hidden from Google — it is the tail of a paid transaction and should never be a landing page — so it is not a search result headline and there is no description to write.

fields.name: architectural
fields.label: After an Architectural Feasibility deposit
fields.description: What someone sees after paying the 50% deposit on the architect-led feasibility. This is the version most buyers see.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line beside the tick.

fields.name: steps
fields.label: What happens next
fields.description: The numbered list under the button. The numbers are counted from the order of this list. Someone has just paid, so every line here is a promise made at the worst possible moment to break one.

fields.name: automated
fields.label: After an Automated Site Feasibility payment
fields.description: What someone sees after paying for the £49.99 automated appraisal in full. It differs from the version above in more than tone: there is no architect review and no validation call at this tier, so do not copy those promises across.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line beside the tick.

fields.name: steps
fields.label: What happens next
fields.description: The numbered list under the button. One of these lines quotes the £49.99 fee: the number is wording only and does not change what anyone is charged, so ask the developer to move both together if the price ever changes.

fields.name: support
fields.label: "Something to send us?" card
fields.description: The bordered card at the bottom, shown after either purchase. The email address itself is set in code so the link and the words it shows can never disagree.

fields.name: linkLabel
fields.label: Case study link text
fields.description: The second link, into a worked example. Where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.description: This line quotes the £15.99 entry price. If a price ever changes, it has to change in code as well — ask the developer rather than editing the number here on its own.

fields.name: products
fields.label: The four products
fields.description: The product ladder at the top of the page. Prices, links and the order of the four are set in code — reordering or removing an item here will not change the page.

fields.name: recommendedLabel
fields.label: Badge on the preferred product
fields.description: The small badge on the Architectural Feasibility card. Ed asked for the architect-led product to be the visually preferred option, labelled explicitly.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Product (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which card this copy belongs to. Read-only: changing it would stop the card reading this text.

fields.name: cta
fields.label: Link label
fields.description: The wording of the link at the bottom of the card. Where it goes is set in code.

fields.name: turnaround
fields.label: Turnaround line
fields.description: The small line above the link, e.g. "5 working days". This is a promise to the customer — leave it blank for products that do not make one.

fields.name: vatNote
fields.label: Footnote under the products
fields.description: Ed's final brief asks for this stated once for the whole ladder rather than repeated on every card.

fields.name: calculator
fields.label: Fee calculator: introduction
fields.description: The copy above the calculator. The questions inside it, and the fee it works out, are code — they follow Ed's pricing brief and are checked against it.

fields.name: lede
fields.label: Supporting paragraph
fields.description: Says how many questions there are. The calculator currently asks seven, so keep the two in step if a question is ever added or removed.

fields.name: feeFactors
fields.label: What affects your fee
fields.description: The list of things that move the fee. Ed's final brief replaced the published fee tables with the factors alone: the customer sees exactly what they will pay in the calculator, without the pricing engine behind it being public. Adding amounts back here would undo that decision.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Factor
fields.description: A few words. These render as pills across the page, so a long sentence will not sit well.

fields.name: footnote
fields.label: Closing line
fields.description: The note about several factors at once routing to an Expert Session. That threshold is enforced in code.

fields.name: comparison
fields.label: Automated vs architect-led
fields.description: The two-card comparison. The prices shown on the cards are set in code so they cannot drift from what the site charges.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading
fields.description: This heading quotes both prices. If a price ever changes it must change in code too, so treat the numbers here as something to update alongside the developer, not on their own.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: Quotes the £49.99 price; see the note on the comparison heading before changing the number.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Heading
fields.description: Also quotes the £49.99 price.

fields.name: text
fields.label: Inclusion
fields.description: This list is what the appraisal actually produces. Only add a line the report really contains.

fields.name: boundary
fields.label: What it does not include
fields.description: Ed asked for this boundary stated plainly rather than buried: the automated appraisal has no drawings and no architect. Softening it invites the complaint it exists to prevent.

fields.name: reviews
fields.label: Reviews section
fields.description: Only the heading of the reviews band on this page. The reviews themselves live under "Reviews (Trustpilot)", and the supporting line and link label come from Site Settings.

fields.name: seo
fields.label: Search engine listing
fields.description: Not shown on the page. This is the title and summary Google shows in its results.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so this is just the page name.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: Around 150 to 160 characters. Google cuts off anything longer.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "Contact". Around 50 characters works best.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small grey word above the headline.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Supporting paragraph
fields.description: Names the ways to get in touch: Jodi's calendar, the enquiry form, one address and one number. If a route is ever added or dropped, this line has to be re-read.

fields.name: expertSession
fields.label: Expert session card
fields.description: The green book-a-call card. Jodi's live Calendly calendar sits inside it; the calendar itself and its link are set in code. These three lines introduce it.

fields.name: personName
fields.label: Name
fields.description: Also sets the initial shown in the circle.

fields.name: pitch
fields.label: Pitch
fields.description: The paragraph beside the calendar.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "Expertise". Around 50 characters works best.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the top of /conversions, above the five sector cards.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the headline.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Standfirst
fields.description: The short paragraph under the headline. Ed's August 2026 final brief, section 06, asked for this page to be a genuine overview rather than a redirect into Commercial to Residential, so this line has to say what the five have in common.

fields.name: shared
fields.label: Wording shared by all five sector pages
fields.description: These appear on Commercial to Residential, HMO, Mixed-Use, High-End Residential and Co-Living & Large HMO alike, not on this page. Editing one here changes it on all five at once, which is the point: they are one sentence shown five times. You can also click any of them on a sector page and land back in this form.

fields.name: opportunityEyebrow
fields.label: Opportunity eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the opening paragraph of every sector page.

fields.name: challengesEyebrow
fields.label: Risks eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the risks section.

fields.name: challengesHeading
fields.label: Risks heading (first line)
fields.description: The sector name is added on a second line in green, with a full stop, so this reads "The Risks Unique To" then "HMO." — write it as the start of that sentence, with no punctuation at the end.

fields.name: solveEyebrow
fields.label: Deliverables eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the four deliverable cards.

fields.name: solveHeading
fields.label: Deliverables heading (first line)
fields.description: Finished by the sector name in green on the line below, the same way as the risks heading: "Built For" then "HMO." No punctuation at the end.

fields.name: ctaHeading
fields.label: Closing heading
fields.description: The heading on the band near the bottom that asks for the enquiry.

fields.name: ctaBody
fields.label: Closing paragraph
fields.description: States the five-day turnaround and the fixed fee, both of which are promises the practice then has to keep. Check with Ed before changing either.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: Used by both buttons on every sector page — the one in the header and the one at the bottom — so the two cannot end up saying different things. Where they go is set in code.

fields.name: otherExpertiseEyebrow
fields.label: Cross-links eyebrow
fields.description: The grey line above the row of links to the other four sectors at the very bottom. Those links are the two-way linking between Expertise pages from Ed's August 2026 final brief; their labels are each sector's own name.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. Unlike most pages on the site, this one is used exactly as typed, so keep "| Thistle Architecture" on the end. Around 60 characters works best.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Sector name
fields.description: The small green line above the headline — the short name for this kind of work, e.g. "HMO". It is reused in four other places: the green second line of "The Risks Unique To…" and "Built For…" further down this page, the card on the Expertise overview, and the links to this page from the other four. Keep it short enough to read as the end of those sentences.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: The only h1 on the page, and what Google reads as the subject of it. Ed's August 2026 final brief asked for these to lead with what someone would actually search for ("HMO Architects & Feasibility Specialists") rather than with a slogan; the slogan moved into the paragraph underneath.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Standfirst
fields.description: The short paragraph under the headline.

fields.name: opportunity
fields.label: "The Opportunity" section
fields.description: The white band under the header: one paragraph, then three figures.

fields.name: copy
fields.label: Paragraph
fields.description: Why this kind of scheme is worth doing at all, put in the reader's terms.

fields.name: stats
fields.label: Figures
fields.description: The three cards under the paragraph. Every one is a public claim about what this kind of scheme delivers — a yield, a decision period, a unit count — so only put a figure here you could evidence if a client asked. The row is built for three; a fourth will not sit evenly.

fields.name: label
fields.label: What it measures
fields.description: The small green line, e.g. "Typical room count".

fields.name: value
fields.label: Figure
fields.description: The large text underneath, e.g. "5 to 9".

fields.name: challenges
fields.label: "What Is Hard" section
fields.description: The risks specific to this sector, listed with an amber warning marker against each. This is the section that shows a reader we have done this before, so keep each one particular to this kind of building — a risk that would be true of any project says nothing. Three on most pages, four on Co-Living & Large HMO.

fields.name: extraSection
fields.label: Extra section (two pages only)
fields.description: The photo-and-text band between the risks and the deliverables. Only two pages have one — Commercial to Residential explains Class MA, HMO points at HMO Checker — and whether a page has this band is set in code, because it also decides how the pale and white bands alternate down the rest of the page. Filling this in on one of the other three will not make it appear; ask a developer.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Paragraphs
fields.description: One box per paragraph, in the order they read. Several of these state rules that change — the 56-day prior approval period, the March 2024 removal of the floorspace cap and the vacancy test, the £15.99 HMO Checker report — so check them against the current position before republishing, and the price against hmochecker.co.uk.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Photograph
fields.description: Leave blank to keep the standing photograph of Beauchamp House, the period office building we converted to flats, which is what the Class MA band uses.

fields.name: imageAlt
fields.label: Photograph description (alt text)
fields.description: Read aloud to blind visitors and used by Google; it is never shown on the page. Describe what is actually in the photograph, and change it whenever you change the photograph.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Link label
fields.description: The green link at the end of the section. Where it goes is set in code — the free Class MA Checker on this site, hmochecker.co.uk from the HMO page — so the wording here has to keep matching the destination.

fields.name: deliverableHighlights
fields.label: "How We Solve It" cards
fields.description: Four of the five feasibility deliverables, each with one line saying what it means for this sector. The card's title and its main description are the deliverable's own wording, shared with the feasibility package page and edited there; the grey line at the bottom of the card is the only part this page owns. Rows cannot usefully be added or removed here — each one names a deliverable, and that name is set in code.

fields.name: deliverableId
fields.label: Deliverable (fixed)
fields.description: Which of the five feasibility deliverables this card is about. Set in code, and read-only: changing it would leave your line underneath attached to a different deliverable, or to none at all.

fields.name: forThisType
fields.label: What it means for this sector
fields.description: The grey line at the bottom of the card, under the divider.

fields.name: relatedCaseStudy
fields.label: Related case study
fields.description: The single study featured near the bottom of this page. Picked from the case studies rather than typed, so it cannot point at one that does not exist. Leave it empty and the section is left out of the page entirely rather than rendering blank.

fields.name: relatedCaseStudyNote
fields.label: Why this project
fields.description: Optional. One or two sentences under the case study heading saying why this project is the right proof for this page. Used on the mixed-use page, where the featured scheme keeps a shop below an HMO and a reader might otherwise take it for a plain HMO job. Leave empty on pages where the fit is obvious.

fields.name: faqs
fields.label: Questions & answers
fields.description: The accordion near the bottom of the page. Ed's August 2026 final brief: "Replace repeated generic feasibility FAQs with sector-specific planning/design questions." These are the questions a buyer of THIS kind of building actually asks; the generic price and turnaround questions are answered elsewhere on the site. Emptying the list falls the page back to that generic set rather than leaving the section blank. The first question is open when the page loads, so put the one most people ask first. Edited in this form only — the accordion is shared with the home and feasibility pages, so it has no click-to-edit marker yet.

fields.name: answer
fields.label: Answer
fields.description: Several of these quote a threshold set nationally or by the council — two years in Class E use, five occupants for mandatory licensing, six for the small-HMO limit. Check any of those still hold before changing them, and keep the hedging that is there on purpose ("it depends entirely on the local authority"): these answers get read as advice.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "Blog". This does not affect the category pages, which write their own.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small grey line above the headline.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: The only h1 on the page. Search engines read it as what the page is about, so keep it descriptive rather than clever.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Standfirst
fields.description: The first sentence under the headline. The page adds a second sentence after it counting the articles currently published, so do not type a number here — it would be out of date the next time an article goes up. Because the paragraph on the page is this sentence plus that count, it is the one field on these three pages you cannot click on the page to edit; edit it here.

fields.name: allLabel
fields.label: First category chip
fields.description: The chip that clears the filter and shows every article. Currently "All". The chips after it are the category names carried on the articles themselves, and each one is also the address of its own category page, so they are not editable here.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "Feasibility Studies".

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small grey line above the headline.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: The only h1 on the page. Search engines read it as what the page is about, so keep it descriptive rather than clever.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Standfirst
fields.description: The short paragraph under the headline.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically, so type just the page name, e.g. "Completed Projects".

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small grey line above the headline.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: The only h1 on the page. Search engines read it as what the page is about, so keep it descriptive rather than clever.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Standfirst
fields.description: The short paragraph under the headline.

fields.name: allLabel
fields.label: First filter chip
fields.description: The chip that clears the filter and shows every project. Currently "All".

fields.name: typeLabels
fields.label: Conversion type chips
fields.description: Renames the filter chips above the grid. Which chips exist, what order they come in, which projects each one shows, and the count beside it are all set in code — this changes only what a visitor reads. A chip whose row is deleted here keeps its standing label rather than disappearing.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Filter (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which chip this is, and appears in the page address while that filter is on. Read-only: a key matching no chip silently does nothing.

fields.name: footnote
fields.label: Note under the grid
fields.description: The small print below the projects. It credits HMO Designers for the projects that practice delivered, which is a factual attribution rather than marketing copy — keep it true if you reword it.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Title
fields.description: What the job was, not the address — e.g. “Six-Bed HMO To Thirteen”. On a new study the web address is built from this.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Type of case study
fields.description: Which of the two lists it belongs to. It also decides which layout the page uses.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.description: Town and county, e.g. “Croydon, South London”. Never the full address.

fields.name: tag
fields.label: Category badge
fields.description: The small pill over the image, e.g. “HMO”. Two or three words at most.

fields.name: buildingType
fields.label: Building type
fields.description: What the building is now, e.g. “Existing dwelling (C3)”.

fields.name: desc
fields.label: Summary
fields.description: One or two sentences: what the building was, and what the job did with it.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Main image
fields.description: The picture beside the title and on every card. On a completed project this must be a real photograph.

fields.name: caption
fields.label: Caption
fields.description: A short line under the main image. Used for "Visualisation" on the pages whose main image is a CGI of a building not yet built (Ed, 9 September 2026), so a reader is not shown a render as a photograph. Leave empty for a photograph or a drawing.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: How to fit it

options.label: Drawing — show it whole, never cropped
Photograph — fill the frame, crop if needed

fields.description: A drawing is shown complete on a white ground, because cropping one cuts off the part that matters. A photograph fills its frame instead, cropping to fit. Every existing image is set to Drawing, which is how the site has always shown them — switching one to Photograph will crop it, so change it only when you want that.

fields.name: listing
fields.label: Where it appears
fields.description: How this study is placed and labelled in the two lists.

fields.name: order
fields.label: Position in the list
fields.description: Lower numbers come first. Completed projects list in this order. Feasibility studies list newest first by their date, and this only decides the order between studies with the same date or no date at all. Leave gaps (10, 20, 30) so a new one can be slotted in.

fields.name: provenance
fields.label: Who did the work
fields.description: Only if another Thistle Group practice did the work, e.g. “By HMO Designers”. Blank for our own.

fields.name: recommendation
fields.label: Recommendation badge
fields.description: Feasibility studies only. Blank if it did not end in one verdict.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Build status
fields.description: The stage shown as a badge on the card and the page. Blank means Complete. Set it here, per project; nothing else has to change.

fields.name: alsoProject
fields.label: Also list under Projects
fields.description: For a feasibility study whose scheme has moved on, so it appears in the Projects list as well as the studies, with the stage above as its badge. Axis House, which went to planning in March 2026, is the case this exists for.

fields.name: conversionTypes
fields.label: Conversion types
fields.description: Which filters this appears under on the Completed Projects page.

fields.name: facts
fields.label: Key facts
fields.description: The band of facts under the page header. All optional.

fields.name: stats
fields.label: Headline facts
fields.description: The three figures on the card, for a completed project or a study not yet on the template. A study with a Key information table below takes its card figures from that table instead (the first three rows that are not the route, the date or the risk), so the card cannot disagree with the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: What it is
fields.description: The small grey line, e.g. "Bedrooms, all en suite".

fields.name: value
fields.label: The figure
fields.description: The larger line underneath, e.g. "13".

fields.name: planningRoute
fields.label: Planning route
fields.description: e.g. “Full planning (Sui Generis)”. Blank if no route was settled.

fields.name: completionDate
fields.label: Date
fields.description: A month and year only, e.g. "June 2026". Never a stage word: "On site" and "Complete" belong in Build status, and putting them here made pages read "Completed: On site" (item 88).

fields.name: unitsBefore
fields.label: Units before
fields.description: Left half of the before-and-after figure, e.g. “3-bed house”.

fields.name: unitsAfter
fields.label: Units after
fields.description: Right half of the same figure, e.g. “7-bed HMO”.

fields.name: writeup
fields.label: Write-up (older layout)
fields.description: Only used where the two templates below are left empty.

fields.name: challenge
fields.label: The Challenge
fields.description: Older layout only. What the client was up against.

fields.name: approach
fields.label: Our Approach
fields.description: Older layout only. What we actually did.

fields.name: outcome
fields.label: The Outcome
fields.description: Older layout only. What the client ended up with.

fields.name: galleryImages
fields.label: Drawings and photographs
fields.description: Sketch options on a study; the gallery at the foot of the page on a project.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: How to fit it

options.label: Drawing — show it whole, never cropped
Photograph — fill the frame, crop if needed

fields.description: A drawing is shown complete on a white ground; a photograph fills its frame and may be cropped at the edges.

fields.name: feasibility
fields.label: Feasibility study write-up
fields.description: The full feasibility template. Filling this in replaces the older three-section write-up above. Leave it empty on a study not written up this way — an empty template reads worse than the older layout.

fields.name: keyInfo
fields.label: Key project information
fields.description: The band of figures straight under the page header. Six is what the row is built for; a seventh wraps onto a second line. These replace the standard fact band rather than sitting beside it, so anything the reader needs — bedrooms, room sizes, communal space, planning route, key risk, date — belongs here.

fields.name: label
fields.label: What it is
fields.description: The small grey line, e.g. "Planning route".

fields.name: value
fields.label: The figure
fields.description: The larger line underneath, e.g. "Full planning, sui generis".

fields.name: indicativeValue
fields.label: Indicative end value
fields.description: Optional single line under the band, printed as "Indicative end value: …". A range is fine ("£600,000 to £680,000"). Only fill this in where the report actually put a number on it; the figure is read as a claim about a real building.

fields.name: brief
fields.label: 01 The Brief
fields.description: The question the client asked, in their terms. Usually one sentence, often phrased as a question.

fields.name: found
fields.label: 02 What We Found
fields.description: The findings: what the building will take, what the policy says, what the precedents are.

fields.name: recommendation
fields.label: 03 Our Recommendation
fields.description: What we told them to do. Separate from the Go / No-Go badge above, which is only the one-word version of this.

fields.name: sketchCaption
fields.label: Caption under the sketch
fields.description: The line under "The Proposed Layout", describing what the drawing shows. Where two options were drawn, say what each one is — the reader is looking at a carousel.

fields.name: guidance
fields.label: Guidance reviewed
fields.description: The small grey line at the foot of "What The Client Received", naming the standards the study was checked against. Left off where no single document governed it.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Wording
fields.description: House style includes the prefix, e.g. "Official guidance reviewed: Croydon HMO space standards".

fields.name: href
fields.label: Link (optional)
fields.description: A web address for the document, if there is a stable public one. With a link the line becomes clickable and opens in a new tab; without one it is plain text. Nothing currently uses this — do not link to a council PDF that will move.

fields.name: decision
fields.label: The Decision
fields.description: The paragraph under "The Decision", near the foot of the page. This is the one that gets read: the honest summary of whether the scheme works and what it has to survive.

fields.name: roadmap
fields.label: Recommended roadmap
fields.description: The numbered steps under the decision, in order. Three or four words each — they are labels on a sequence, not instructions. The order is the whole point of the list, so drag rather than retype.

fields.name: projectStory
fields.label: Project story
fields.description: The completed-project template: the write-up, the existing-and-proposed pair, and the stages down the page. Replaces the older three-section write-up above.

fields.name: summary
fields.label: The write-up
fields.description: The opening write-up, one paragraph per box, in order. The first paragraph prints larger than the rest, so it wants to be the one that says what the building was and what it became. These are Ed's own words from Project Explanations.docx.

fields.name: beforeAfter
fields.label: Existing and proposed
fields.description: Two photographs side by side near the top of the page, labelled "Existing" and "Completed". Ed's template puts it there on purpose: a reader who stops after the first screen should still see the scale of the change. Only fill it in where there is a genuine before photograph — one project has one so far.

fields.name: beforeAlt
fields.label: Before — description (alt text)
fields.description: Read aloud to blind visitors and used by Google; never shown on the page. Describe what is in the photograph. Change it whenever you change the photograph.

fields.name: afterAlt
fields.label: After — description (alt text)
fields.description: The same, for the completed photograph.

fields.name: sections
fields.label: Stages
fields.description: The stages of the project, in order down the page, alternating light and white backgrounds. Ed's template is explicit that a stage goes in only where there is good material for it, rather than padding the page with placeholders — so a project carries the stages it can evidence and stops there. A stage with one picture shows it wide; two or more go in a grid.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Stage heading
fields.description: e.g. "The Existing Building", "Construction", "The Completed House".

fields.name: caption
fields.label: Introduction
fields.description: A sentence or two under the heading, before the pictures. Optional.

fields.name: images
fields.label: Pictures
fields.description: Photographs and visualisations for this stage. They are cropped to a common shape so the grid lines up, so avoid anything that loses its subject at the edges.

fields.name: alt
fields.label: Description (alt text)
fields.description: Read aloud to blind visitors and used by Google; never shown on the page. Describe what is in the picture, and say when it is a visualisation rather than a photograph.

fields.name: seo
fields.label: Search listing
fields.description: How the page reads in Google. Both can be left blank.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: Blank uses the title above, which is usually right.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: Blank uses the summary above. Google cuts it off around 155 characters.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: The headline at the top of the article, and on its card on /blog. On a NEW article the web address is built from this, so get it right before saving; on an existing one the address is already fixed and changing the headline leaves it alone.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: Optional, and blank on nearly every article: leave it empty and Google shows the headline above. Fill it in only when the search listing has to differ from the headline. Unlike the other pages on the site, what you type here is used exactly as typed, so put "| Thistle Architecture" on the end yourself.

fields.name: excerpt
fields.label: Summary
fields.description: Does two jobs: it is the paragraph under the headline on the card on /blog, and it is the grey summary under the title in Google. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters, so put the point first.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Main photograph
fields.description: Shown wide at the top of the article and again on the card on /blog. Landscape, near 2:1 — a portrait shot is cropped top and bottom. There is no separate description field for it: the headline above is read aloud to blind visitors in its place.

fields.name: date
fields.label: Published date
fields.description: Written out as it should read on the page, e.g. "January 17, 2025". Keep that format — it is also the date given to Google as the article's publication date, and a date it cannot read is no date at all.

fields.name: updated
fields.label: Updated date
fields.description: Optional. Fill this in when an article has been genuinely revised and the line under the byline gains "· Updated <date>". Same format as the published date. Leave it blank rather than refreshing it to look current: Google is told this is when the article last changed.

fields.name: readTime
fields.label: Reading time
fields.description: The small grey line beside the category, e.g. "5 min read". Typed rather than counted, so it is worth checking after a long addition. Roughly 200 words a minute.

fields.name: category
fields.label: Category
fields.description: Decides which category page the article is filed under, and the chip shown under the headline. Please ask a developer before moving an article: the category pages are still built from the list in code, so a change made only here would leave the chip and the category page disagreeing.

fields.name: author
fields.label: Author
fields.description: The byline under the headline and the card at the foot of the article. Whoever is named here is credited to Google as the author, so it should be a real person at the practice.

fields.name: role
fields.label: Job title
fields.description: Shown beside the date, and again under the author card as "<title>, Thistle Architecture" — so type the title on its own, without the practice name.

fields.name: initials
fields.label: Initials
fields.description: The two letters shown beside the byline when there is no photograph. Not worked out from the name, so change it when the name changes.

fields.name: photo
fields.label: Photograph
fields.description: Head and shoulders, square. Shown beside the byline and on the card at the foot of the article, in place of the initials. Leave it empty and the initials are used instead, which is how every article looked before this field existed.

fields.name: bio
fields.label: Short bio
fields.description: Two or three sentences on the card at the foot of the article, saying why this person is worth reading on this subject. Google weighs author expertise, so write it about their experience rather than about the practice. Leave it empty and the card shows the name and job title only.

fields.name: linkedin
fields.label: LinkedIn profile
fields.description: Optional. A link on the author card, which gives Google a second, independent source for who this person is. Paste the full address, starting https://.

fields.name: content
fields.label: Article
fields.description:
The body of the article, one block per box, in order. A block is normally a paragraph. It can also be:

• a heading — start the line with "## " (these are the ones that appear in the "Jump to" list at the top)
• a smaller heading — start the line with "### "
• a bullet — start the line with "- ". Consecutive bullets become one list.
• a link inside a paragraph — [the words you want to show](https://example.com), or [the words](/pricing) for a page on this site
• a picture — ![description of the picture](/images/blog/example.jpg)

Tables are one box per row, written with pipes: | Column | Column | with a | --- | --- | row underneath the headings.

Use the drag handle to reorder blocks. Anything that is not one of the above is a plain paragraph.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Search result title
fields.description: The tab title and the blue headline in Google. Unlike the other pages, this one is used exactly as typed, so keep "| Thistle Architecture" on the end. Around 60 characters works best.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: Search result description
fields.description: The grey summary under the headline in Google. Not shown anywhere on the page. Google cuts it off after roughly 155 characters.

fields.name: hero
fields.label: Page header
fields.description: The pale band at the very top of the page.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small grey line above the headline. It is the name of the tool, e.g. "HMO Valuation Calculator".

fields.name: description
fields.label: Standfirst
fields.description: The short paragraph under the headline. It tells the reader what the tool will ask them for and how long it takes, so if the tool ever changes, this has to change with it.

fields.name: panels
fields.label: Calculator panel headings
fields.description: The headings on the two white panels either side of the calculators. The Class MA checker has no panels, so leave this blank on that one.

fields.name: note
fields.label: Note under the inputs
fields.description: Small grey text under the input panel explaining what the starting figures assume. Only the HMO calculator has one. The starting figures themselves are set in code, so this text describes them rather than setting them — if one is ever adjusted, a developer has to bring the two back into line.

fields.name: outcomes
fields.label: Result messages
fields.description: What the tool says for each result it can reach. The tool decides which one to show; you are editing the words, not the rule. Every threshold quoted in them ("under 10%", "between 10 and 25%") is set in code, so changing a number here changes what the reader is told, not when they are told it, and the two would then disagree.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Result (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which result this message belongs to. Read-only, and entries must not be added or removed.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Headline
fields.description: On the calculators this is the one-word verdict badge ("Viable"). On the Class MA checker it is the full sentence across the top of the result card.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Explanation
fields.description: The paragraph under the headline. This is the part that turns a number into advice, so it is worth more care than anything else on the page.

fields.name: emailOffer
fields.label: Email offer
fields.description: The box under the Class MA result that asks for an email address. The two calculators do not have one, so leave this blank on those.

fields.name: heading
fields.label: Offer heading
fields.description: This has to name something that genuinely gets sent. The prior-approval checklist goes out on the Formspree autoresponse (formspree.json); promising anything else here means someone has to build it first.

fields.name: disclaimer
fields.label: Disclaimer line
fields.description: The centred grey line under the tool. It is the only thing on the page saying the result is an indication rather than a professional opinion, which is what stops a free tool reading as advice the practice stands behind. Have it checked before rewording it, and do not remove it.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.label: Button label
fields.description: Used by every "Get Your Fixed Fee" button on this page — the one in the result card and the one at the bottom — so the two cannot end up saying different things. Where the button goes is set in code.

fields.name: closing
fields.label: Closing section
fields.description: The white band at the bottom, between the tool and the standard CTA band.

fields.name: headingAccent
fields.label: Heading, second line
fields.description: Shown in green under the first line. Two fields because a single string cannot carry the colour change.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Paragraph
fields.description: States the five-day turnaround and the fixed fee, both of which are promises the practice then has to keep. Check with Ed before changing either.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Page title
fields.description: The large heading at the top of the page. The full stop at the end is house style across the site — "Privacy Policy.", not "Privacy Policy".

fields.name: lastUpdated
fields.label: Last updated
fields.description: The date only, as it should read — e.g. "February 2026". The words "Last updated:" are added by the page, so do not type them here. Edited in this form rather than by clicking the page, because the line on the page includes that fixed label as well as the date.

fields.name: sections
fields.label: Sections
fields.description: The body of the document, in order. This is legal wording: a change here changes what the practice has committed to. Have any edit checked by whoever advises on the contract before publishing, and correct clauses that are wrong rather than rewriting ones that merely read awkwardly.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Body
fields.description: One paragraph, or several separated by a blank line. Several of these state a specific commitment — the 7-year retention period, the limitation of liability, the England and Wales jurisdiction, the privacy@ address people are told to write to. Check any of those still hold before changing them.

fields.name: bullets
fields.label: Bulleted list
fields.description: Optional, and shown under the paragraph above. Used by the feasibility disclaimer, where the list of what a report is not has to read as a list rather than as prose.

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Opening paragraph
fields.description: Feasibility disclaimer only. The paragraph between the title and the first numbered section, before any heading.

fields.name: liabilityCap
fields.label: Liability cap
fields.description: Feasibility disclaimer only. The money figure in section 8, written as it should read, e.g. "£25,000". IT IS BLANK UNTIL ED SETS IT, and the page says so in place of the number rather than inventing one. Nobody here can decide this figure.

fields.name: piLimit
fields.label: Professional indemnity limit
fields.description: Feasibility disclaimer only. The limit of indemnity in section 8, e.g. "£1,000,000". Same as above: blank until confirmed, and it must match the actual policy.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: SEO title
fields.description: Shown in the browser tab and as the headline in Google results, not on the page. The site name is appended automatically.

fields.name: metaDescription
fields.label: SEO description
fields.description: The grey summary under the title in Google results. Not shown on the page. Around 150 characters is the most that gets displayed.

fields.name: author
fields.label: Reviewer name
fields.description: Exactly as published on Trustpilot. Do not tidy or abbreviate.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Review title
fields.description: The headline as published, where the review has one.

fields.name: quote
fields.label: Quote
fields.description: VERBATIM EXCERPT — do not reword, reorder or correct, including original typos. This is a real person’s published review; changing it misrepresents them. Shorten only by trimming whole sentences from the start or end.

fields.name: date
fields.label: Date (as displayed)
fields.description: Human-readable, e.g. "30 June 2026".

fields.name: datePublished
fields.label: Date (machine-readable)
fields.description: ISO form of the same date, e.g. "2026-06-30". Used for schema.org markup, so it must match the displayed date.

fields.name: rating
fields.label: Star rating
fields.description: Out of 5. Must match the published review.

fields.name: topics
fields.label: Topics
fields.description: Which pages this review is eligible to appear on. Structural, not copy — it controls placement, not wording.

fields.name: order
fields.label: Display order
fields.description: Lower numbers appear first.

fields.name: metaTitle
fields.label: Browser tab title
fields.description: Shown in the browser tab. This page is hidden from Google on purpose, so this is not a search listing — it is just what the tab says while you have the page open. "| Thistle Architecture" is added automatically.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.description: The small green line above the heading.

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Introduction
fields.description: The paragraph under the heading that explains what the three columns are.

fields.name: note
fields.label: Reassurance line
fields.description: The small grey line that says none of this is live yet. Worth keeping accurate: it is the line that stops anyone thinking the AI headshots are already on the site.

fields.name: columns
fields.label: Columns
fields.description: The three options being compared, left to right. Each heading appears twice on the page — once on the key at the top, once as the caption under every photo in that column — so editing it here changes both. There are three columns because there are three sets of photographs; adding a row here would only produce a broken image.

fields.name: key
fields.label: Column (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies which set of photographs this column shows, and is part of each image filename. Read-only: changing it would leave the column with no images.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Heading
fields.description: Keep the A. / B. / C. prefix — the intro paragraph refers to the columns by letter.

fields.name: note
fields.label: Description
fields.description: The explanation on the key at the top of the page. Column C’s says the AI option needs each person’s consent before it goes live; please do not drop that.

fields.name: people
fields.label: People
fields.description: The heading above each row of three photos. These are the five people who were photographed, in the order the page shows them; adding or removing a row here does not add or remove a row of photographs.

fields.name: slug
fields.label: Person (fixed)
fields.description: Identifies whose photographs this row shows, and is part of each image filename. Read-only: changing it would leave the row with no images.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.description: Also read aloud to blind visitors as part of each photo description, so it is worth spelling as the person spells it.

description.value: References another document, used as a foreign key
